claim: AWS recommends setting a lifecycle expiration period for your S3 versions, because the recovery point stores all objects and versions in the bucket and storage cost is calculated for all objects in the backup, including objects scheduled for deletion.

evidence.quote: We recommend that you set a lifecycle expiration period for your S3 versions.

All objects (including all versions) in the bucket when the backup begins will be stored in the recovery point (completed backup). These can include the current version of each object, older versions, delete markers, and objects pending lifecycle actions.
The storage cost will be calculated for all objects in the backup, including objects scheduled for deletion (objects that will expire).
